messages:
ryan-support: Heads-up — AcmeCorp hitting repeated 429s on their dedicated pool since yesterday evening after we processed their plan change. They say requests succeed then get bursts of throttles every ~5m window.

julia-sre: Can you paste a sample request/response with headers? also which dedicated pool id?

ryan-support: Pool is dp-az-west-03. Example response they sent: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 60
X-Rate-Limit-Limit: 600
X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 0
X-Rate-Limit-Window: 300
```
Body: {"error":"rate limit exceeded","code":"RATE_UNIT_EXCEEDED"}
```

acme-sre: Confirmed. We saw periodic throttles in prod starting ~2024-10-12T18:04:00Z after billing switched to the new committed plan. Token usage stayed around normal. Looks correlated to a scheduler tick.

mike-platform: Interesting — X-Rate-Limit-Window showing 300 (5m). That header comes from per-tenant rate window calculation. Billing change might have updated units but scheduler may have reinterpreted denom (minutes vs hours).

julia-sre: Repro steps request: can Acme run a simple curl loop to show pattern? e.g. 
```
for i in $(seq 1 120); do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACME_KEY>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=meta-7b"; sleep 2; done
```

acme-sre: Running that now. Attaching trimmed logs when it hits 429s.

acme-sre: Log snippet: 
```
2024-10-12T18:03:10Z 200 OK X-Remaining: 5
2024-10-12T18:03:12Z 200 OK X-Remaining: 4
...
2024-10-12T18:07:10Z 429 X-Remaining: 0 Window-reset-in: 180
2024-10-12T18:07:12Z 200 OK X-Remaining: 5
```

olivia-billing: I looked at the plan change: we migrated them from a per-minute quota (units/min) to a per-hour aggregated quota (units/hour) but the quota-converter job had a rounding flag off, so it wrote a per-minute numeric into the per-hour store. Effectively their committed units were multiplied by 60.

mike-platform: That would cause the system to think they had much higher capacity — why are they getting 429s then?

julia-sre: Two parts: 1) The scheduler that enforces soft windows reads the rate_window value from the rateprofile which was set to 300 (5m) by the platform layering rule for dedicated pools. 2) The quota-allocator's burst calculation uses both the numeric quota and the rate_unit. If the numeric was migrated incorrectly, the rolling replenish token bucket ended up with odd bucket fill/empty cadence causing sawtooth drains where Remaining drops to zero at the end of each 5m window.

acme-sre: So it's not noisy neighbor, it's scheduler/quota mismatch?

julia-sre: Likely. But we should still check for noisy neighbors — if one tenant is aggressively using burst capacity it can cause eviction from quiet pools. However logs show other tenants stable.

mike-platform: Quick checks I ran: 
```
# inspect rateprofile for tenant
GET /internal/tenants/acme/rateprofile
response: {"units":600,"unit_window":"minute"}

# the allocator reads: units=600 window=hour
```
We see the unit_window mismatch.

ryan-support: Customer asks for mitigation — they want traffic back to normal ASAP.

julia-sre: Short-term mitigation: switch their rateprofile to an explicit per-minute window that matches the numeric value OR set a temporary higher per-tenant burst ceiling to smooth transitions. I can flip the profile to per-minute safely.

olivia-billing: I'll push a policy override to map their plan -> per_minute on the policy service for the next 24h. Logging why in case of audit.

mike-platform: Also recommend restarting the quota-allocator worker for dp-az-west-03 to clear stale token buckets: `kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/quota-allocator-dp-az-west-03`. Do after billing override applied.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout restart deployment/quota-allocator-dp-az-west-03 requested by mike-platform.

acme-sre: We applied the curl test again after the override and restart. No 429s in the last 10m — looks stable. Thanks.

julia-sre: Follow-ups: 1) create a test to catch unit_window migrations with rounding=false, 2) add an alert if rate_profile.unit != allocator.read_unit for >1 tenant in a pool, 3) run quota-allocator canary on next deploy. I'll open tickets.

ryan-support: Customer very happy with the quick fix. I'll mark as resolved once dev tickets are linked. :tada:

mike-platform: Filed infra#8762 (unit-window mismatch detector) and infra#8763 (repro harness + canary). Leaving this thread for postmortem notes.

ryan-support: Closing loop — acme says no further 429s, moving to monitoring. Thanks team! :heart:
